newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PLA seeks to bury Tiananmen image with band parade.
newsitem.headline: PLA seeks to bury Tiananmen image with band parade.

text.p: China's People's Liberation Army (PLA), widely feared for massacring unarmed compatriots in Beijing eight years ago, will turn from warriors to musicians when Britain hands Hong Kong to China.
The troops will mingle with the Hong Kong police, boy scouts, girl guides and kung-fu clubs for a spectacular musical parade at next week's handover.
It will be the first time the PLA has performed in Hong Kong or mingled with crowds in this bustling 156-year-old British colony, set to be handed back to China at midnight on Monday.
The PLA will field a 120-strong marching band alongside civic groups, organisers said on Wednesday.

The band from Beijing will perform in Hong Kong's biggest carnival parade, comprising 31 floats and 25 troupes of performers, beneath the glass and marble skyscrapers along Hong Kong Island's harbourfront highways on Tuesday.
The floats will represent colours of the rainbow symbolising confidence in Hong Kong's future prosperity and positive ties with China and the world, organisers said.
Many of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people are worried about having a PLA garrison in the territory after the handover.
They remember the PLA's role in the bloody anti-democracy crackdown in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in 1989.

China has already sent an advance guard of 196 soldiers to Hong Kong to get garrison facilities ready, and a further 500 will arrive on Monday evening. Thousands more are expected to move in some time soon after the sovereignty transfer.
